name: Work_CopyRowToDataPanel
summary: Copies row rowIndex of the 0x8C-byte row table at save work +0x7B3C into the first free row of the 50-entry data-panel table at +0x5FE4. Shop_BuyItem calls it after a purchase so the bought item's row shows up in the panel.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the confident Ui_DataPanel_InsertRowCopy (0.60), whose destination is the 50-row 0x8C-stride table at +0x5FE4, and the named caller Shop_BuyItem supplies the row index; the body shows the source table base +0x7B3C with the same 0x8C stride, so the old 'InsertRowTableCopy' wording is replaced by the actual source and destination.

name: Work_AreAllDataPanelRowsUsed
summary: Returns true when none of the 50 rows of the data-panel table at work+0x5FE4 is free: it walks the 0x8C-byte rows, counts the ones with a short name, a non-zero key and a valid +0x88 word, and compares the count with 50.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly (the readable C stops at the wcslen call) shows the same 50-iteration, 0x8C-stride loop over work+0x5FE4 that the confident Ui_DataPanel_InsertRowCopy fills, and the tail 'cmp r6,#0x32; moveq r0,#1' returns a bool 'all 50 rows used' - the old name was wrong about both the return type and the table.

name: ActorActionSeq_CanAdvance
summary: Answers whether the action sequence may move on: it counts the actors whose per-actor report (virtual +0x14) is finished and, when not all are, compares the per-character counters at +0x9A5/+0x9A6 with the actor count. Returns 1 when the sequence may advance.
evidence: NEW: the four callers are the field steppers (Field_ActorActionSeq_StepEntryA/RunExtraEntry/AppendEntries) AND the battle stepper Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateActorStep, so the 'Field_' prefix is wrong; the fallback to the per-character counters +0x9A5/+0x9A6 shows it answers 'may advance', not 'are all actors ready'.

name: ActorActionSeq_AdvanceAction
summary: Advances the sequence's action cursor: derives the per-character repetition limit from +0x4ED (character ids 5 and 0x24 have their own rules), bumps the action counter +0x9A6 and the per-character index +0x87D when the current slot count reaches the limit, and returns 1 when it moved.
evidence: NEW: same caller set as 0x003C0BCC (three field steppers plus Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateActorStep), so the 'Field_' prefix is wrong; the fully readable body bumps +0x9A6/+0x87D and returns 1 only when the limit was reached, which matches 'advance the action cursor'.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_PickRandomReadyActor
summary: Counts the actors whose virtual +0x10 reports ready, rolls a battle-RNG index in [0, count-1] and returns the actor slot at that ordinal. The command and round code use it to pick which ready actor acts.
evidence: NEW: the body rolls func_001CA474(battleWork+0x4218, 0, count-1) - the battle RNG roll documented in FACTS.md - and then returns the actor at that ordinal, so it picks a RANDOM ready actor; the old 'FindNextReadyActor' was wrong on both counts (the range starts at 0 and the choice is random).

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_GetDisplayId
summary: Returns a small id for the unit the object currently points at: for ordinary units it is byte +0x147 of the action record selected by the u16 at self+0x1230 (falling back to the unit's +0xE88 when that byte is 0xFF); for special units it forwards to the unit's virtual +0x78 with a per-slot byte from self->f_50+0xB0FA.
evidence: NEW: the two confident callers Battle_PartyMember_GetDisplayId/_Copy save and restore the unit byte +0xBF7 around the call (0x00161D90/0x00161FE8), so the call has a side effect and the wrappers only want the returned id; the id itself comes from action record +0x147 (0x0063FD24, 0x19C-byte rows) with the unit's +0xE88 as fallback, so 'display id' is still only the callers' word - kept maybe_.

name: Ui_DiveForm_UpdatePage
summary: Advances one page of the dive form: updates the page widget at +0x210 from the state block at page+0x35C and, once the widget reports completion, pops the pane and hides the form.
evidence: NEW: both follow-up callees are the confident Ui_DiveForm_PopPane and Ui_DiveForm_SetVisible, and the completion test 0x0062F680 is a one-instruction getter ([r0+0x28] == 0), so the page-update-then-close reading holds.

name: maybe_Model_ApplyColorVariant
summary: Picks a colour variant for one slot: when the slot byte at self[*self+0xD] is still 0xFF it reads three (or the second three) bytes of the data row selected by *self, chooses one with Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng and stores the mapped palette byte from 0x00727397.
evidence: The body is damaged (unaff_r5 is the row-index register), so neither the row index nor the destination slot can be read; the only named callee is Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng and the byte table at 0x00727397 is unnamed, so the colour-variant reading stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateInBoxSet
summary: Per-frame update of a field actor that first queries the scene box set at the actor's position (work->f_50), then runs the model's virtual +0x9C update and the common Field_Actor_UpdateBehaviour. The box query's result is discarded, so it is probably used for its side effect.
evidence: No caller and no string names the action, and the old 'DragonJumpAction_UpdateCamera' asserted a class and a camera link the body does not show; what is certain is the actor position read (f_28+0x9C..0xA4), the Field_Scene_IsPointInsideBoxSetA query and the Field_Actor_UpdateBehaviour tail, so the name now says only that.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_SelectItem
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemList_SelectItem(void* self, u32 list, char* names)
summary: Selection loop of an item list: writes the chosen index into the row byte +0x1AD, refreshes the category text and the list scroll, and formats the item's name into a message argument (Item_LookupRecord + Message_SetArg + Text_FormatMessageArg) until the confirm helper 0x0064D6E0 reports done.
evidence: The body is heavily damaged (five unaff_* registers, garbled name-index expression), so only the callees can be trusted: Item_LookupRecord, Message_SetArg and Text_FormatMessageArg show it formats an item name, and Ui_ListWidget_ResetToFirstEntry/UpdateScroll show a list; nothing supports the old 'SmithMenu' class, so the name now says only 'item list'.

name: Ui_Menu_StartModeTransition
summary: Starts a menu mode transition: saves func_001F333C() into the UI context (+0x2FAE0), resets the data panel at +0x718, clears the flag word +0x824 and then selects mode 1 (flag 0x10000 plus 0x002CDB5C) when the UI manager's +0xE3C0 state is 3, or mode 3 after a full data-panel reset otherwise; the mode is stored at +0x820.
evidence: NEW: the sibling 0x003F306C is the same tail without the +0x718 panel reset, and both use the confident Ui_DataPanel_Reset and Ui_UiManager_GetInstance, so the mode-selection reading is shared and the extra save/reset is what makes this the transition entry (vtable slot 0x0072CAA0).

name: Ui_Menu_InitModeState
summary: Initialises the menu mode state: clears the flag word at +4 and then selects mode 1 (flag 0x10000 plus 0x002CDB5C) when the UI manager's +0xE3C0 state is 3, or mode 3 after Ui_DataPanel_Reset otherwise; the mode is stored at +0.
evidence: NEW: the named callees Ui_DataPanel_Reset and Ui_UiManager_GetInstance are the whole body, and the sibling 0x003F3030 is the same tail plus the +0x718 panel reset, so the two are the plain and the full mode initialiser.

name: Party_GetReserveMemberId
summary: Returns the character id of the reserve-list entry the panel cursor points at: it walks the 31-entry roster at save work +4, counts the members whose record has bits 0-1 of +4 set, and returns the id whose running count equals the cursor value (virtual +0x88) plus 4 - i.e. the entry after the four on-screen slots. Returns 0xFF when there is none.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers passes the panel's reserve cursor (self[0x7E]) and feeds the result to Menu_SelectPartyPair as the incoming member, and the body compares the running count with 'cursor + 4', so it returns the reserve-list id, not a member 'by position' in general.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_CanSwapMember
signature: u32 Ui_PartyPanel_CanSwapMember(UiPartyPanel* self, u32 skipIndex, u32 memberId)
summary: Swap guard of the party panel: when the incoming member's battle unit reports the virtual +0x10 state, it counts the other existing units (virtual +0x24) and refuses (returns 0) if every one of them is in that state too, so the swap cannot leave the party with nobody outside it. Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers shows the 0xF55 popup on 0.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers shows the 0xF55 error popup exactly when this returns 0 and otherwise calls Menu_SelectPartyPair, which fixes the polarity; the body's 'uVar4 <= uVar5 -> 0' comparison means 'all other existing members are in the +0x10 state', so the old 'CheckOtherMemberAvailability' name described the opposite.

name: Party_ValidateMemberSlots
summary: Returns 1 when the panel's four slot ids (+0x6E..+0x71, -1 = empty) agree with the active party: it counts the filled slots and the roster entries whose record has bits 0-1 of +4 set, and accepts when all four slots are filled or the two counts match.
evidence: NEW: the two unnamed callees are now identified from the disassembly - 0x0066B0E4 is a one-instruction byte getter saveWork[index+4] over the 31-entry roster and 0x0063F8F0 is the 31-row, 0x40-byte roster record lookup whose +4 bits 0-1 mark an active member - so the 'do the visible slots match the active roster' reading holds; the named caller Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmMemberSlots only proceeds when it returns 1.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_HasAvailableMember
summary: Returns 1 as soon as one of the panel's four slot ids resolves to a battle unit whose virtual +0x10 state is 0, i.e. when at least one member in the panel is still usable; returns 0 when all four are missing or in that state.
evidence: NEW: the body returns a bool (1 on the first match), not a member, and the named caller Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmMemberSlots shows the 0xF55 error popup when it returns 0 - so it answers 'is any panel member usable', which the old 'FindFirstUsableMember' name got wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_WriteRowOffset
summary: Fragment of the party-panel row setup: computes a signed row offset from self->f_38->f_c and self->f_28 and writes the low halfword at +6 of a record the decompiler lost (unaff_r7); the rest of the body is bad instruction data.
evidence: Only the prologue survives (halt_baddata, software_interrupt, unaff_r7 destination), so neither the record nor the offset is readable; the single caller is the named Ui_PartyPanel_ConfirmMemberSlots, which keeps the party-panel context but not the role.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateBattleTrigger
summary: Per-frame poll of an object's battle trigger: when the per-map byte at work+0x2A4E6+self->f_298 is 1 or 4 it returns the channel busy state; otherwise it starts the trigger once (flag f_29A, trigger object f_29C) and on later frames calls Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle.
evidence: NEW: the completion call is the confident Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle and the started flag is f_29A on the trigger object at f_29C, so this is the trigger's per-frame poll; the per-map byte table at work+0x2A4E6 is still only inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_List_IsCursorCellFree
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_List_IsCursorCellFree(u32 layout, u32 region, u32 arg3, u32* cell)
summary: Cursor usability test for a 2D layout cell: in text mode it finds the cell with Ui_HitTest_FindCell, rejects it when the occupancy query says so and otherwise defers to maybe_Ui_List_CanMoveCursor; in the other mode it rejects the glyph cell bytes 0, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 0xFF.
evidence: No callers; the two branches test a layout cell (Ui_HitTest_FindCell / maybe_Ui_List_CanMoveCursor) and a glyph cell byte (Font_Atlas_GetGlyphCellByte), so 'free cell' covers both, but the subsystem (UI list vs Field2D map) and the meaning of the rejected glyph bytes stay open.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ChooseDamageNumberFont
summary: Chooses one of five ids for the battle HUD: it popcounts the 31-bit mask at +0x16B0 and returns 0xE89 for 1-2 set bits or 0xEBC for 3+, unless the battle-mode byte (work+0x5C+0x4244) and the per-unit byte +0x16BD select 0xF54, 0xF51 or 0xF50.
evidence: The popcount and the five literal ids are exact and the mode byte is the known work+0x5C+0x4244 flag, but nothing names the ids as fonts - they may be message or effect ids - and the callers (Battle_UpdatePartyWidgets, Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateMain) do not settle it.

name: maybe_Battle_ShowCommandListEntry
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ShowCommandListEntry(BattleScene* self, int entryIndex, int visible)
summary: Shows or hides one row of a battle list: hiding row N (or the 0xFF 'none' row) clears the visible flag of the actor whose id sits at self[N*2+0x498] in the battle actor list, while showing the special row 4 either forwards to the window's virtual +0x60 or to the shared actor action handler depending on the state byte +0x168D.
evidence: NEW: the two named callers (Battle_SpawnUnitModel, Battle_Ui_UpdateActionPopupForUnit) place it in battle-unit display setup rather than in a command list, and the row ids come from the u16 array at self+0x498 and are resolved in the battle actor list at work+0x5C+0x4254, so 'command list' stays unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_ProfileScreen_UpdateSelection
summary: State-machine step of a list window: when no party name is loaded it activates the cursor row, otherwise it picks controller state 4, 5 or 8 for the controller at f_11C depending on whether the field is paused and on the root singleton's mode, then runs the controller.
evidence: No callers; the body only shows the state ids 4/5/8 handed to the controller at f_11C and the Party_GetFirstNameLength test that decides whether a party exists, so the 'ProfileScreen' class and the 'UpdateSelection' role remain guesses.

name: maybe_Ui_ProfileScreen_ConfirmSelection
summary: Confirm step of the same window: when the root singleton reports idle it resets the transform on the save work and then either activates the cursor row (no pending selection at f_29D) or advances the controller at f_11C to state 9.
evidence: No callers; the body shares the f_11C controller and the f_29D field with 0x00466350, so the two are the update and confirm halves of one window, but nothing names that window.

name: Ui_ReleaseHandle
summary: Releases the object a handle slot points at through the UI core's release helper (core->f_C) and clears the slot. Used by the talk-party teardown paths.
evidence: NEW: the singleton is the confident Ui_GetCore and the helper 0x0021F8B8 is the sibling of the confident Ui_List_ReleaseEntries (0x0021F868), so the release goes through the UI core, not a 'Container'; the two named callers Menu_TalkParty_Teardown/ReleaseAll clear their handles with it.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_NotifyMemberModelChanged
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_NotifyMemberModelChanged(PartyWindow* self, PartyModel* model, u32 member)
summary: Clears the f_79 byte on every unit model of the four battle unit lists (work+0x5C+0x428C, stride 0x1C), then sends a {memberId, model, ...} message through the party window's virtual +0x60 and stores the reply at window+4.
evidence: NEW: the named callers Battle_PlayPartyMemberSe and Battle_UnitModel_AdvanceAnimSequence both change which member a model shows, and the body's only effects are the f_79 clear over the four unit lists and the message through self->f_C virtual +0x60 - so 'BindModelAnims' described neither.

name: Field_Object2D_Type0003_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the 2D variant of field object type 3: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x7746EC, sets the two default words at 0x497/0x498, resets the party member slot and zeroes the last word of the 0x1268-byte layout at +0x1264.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Field_ObjectFactory_Type0003 allocates the 0x1268-byte object and calls either the confident Field_Object3D_Ctor (0x00438CE8, the 3D variant) or this function, so this is the 2D variant of the same type; the zero word at +0x1264 is the last field of that 0x1268-byte layout.

name: Battle_Action_GetEffectValue
summary: Returns the action's effect value as a float: special units (+0x10 set) go through Battle_Monster_GetEffectValue, ordinary units convert the action record's u16 fields +0x13C/+0x13E/+0x140/+0x142 to float, each guarded by the flag bytes +0x189/+0x187/+0x185/+0x184.
evidence: NEW: the special-unit branch calls the confident Battle_Monster_GetEffectValue, so the general branch is the same query for ordinary units; the four VectorUnsignedToFloat calls write s0, i.e. the function returns a float, which the old 'GetRowValue' name did not say.

name: Battle_MonsterUI_MeasureText
summary: Measures one monster HUD text: when the message has a format record it builds the layout params, dispatches the formatted text through Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch and returns the measured width multiplied by the layout scale at +0x420.
evidence: NEW: the body returns scale x the width that the confident Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch measures, so it is a measurement helper and the old 'CalcRowHeight' name claimed a height the code never computes; the only caller is the named Battle_TargetMarker_Update.

name: Field_Object_Type1351_Ctor
summary: Constructor of field object type 1351: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x775B74, sets the two default words at 0x497/0x498 and resets the party member slot.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Type1351, and its disassembly shows both allocation branches calling this one constructor, so it is the type's single constructor; the body stores vtable 0x775B74, not the 0x775C54 the old name claimed.

name: maybe_Battle_CommandEntry_Build
summary: Builds or validates one battle command entry and returns whether it is usable; the readable body is only a 1904-byte stack frame plus a lost array constructor, so the field logic is not visible.
evidence: The body is lost (std_ConstructArray is marked noreturn and the rest of the 680-byte function is missing), so only the callers can be trusted: Battle_Command_ResolveVariantCode and Battle_CommandListWindow_IsCursorUsable put it in the command-list path, which supports 'command entry' but not the exact role.

name: Field_ModelSlotEmitter_RefreshFromOwner
summary: Refreshes a field model-slot emitter: it resolves the owner flag from the save work, then walks the ten 0xB8-byte slot records and reconfigures the one whose owner id equals self+0x268 through Field_ModelSlotEmitter_Configure, and finally updates the child object at f_4C.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Field_ModelSlotEmitter_Configure (0.50) is called here for the one of ten 0xB8-byte slot records whose owner id matches self+0x268, exactly as its other caller Field_ModelSlotEmitter_SpawnOne does; the old 'Ui_ListWindow_RefreshCharacterRows' name described a list window the body never touches.

name: maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitHpChange
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitHpChange(BattleUi* self, u32 unit, u32 value)
summary: Applies a damage/heal number to the acting battle unit: it validates the unit's effect state (0x11) and remaining HP, then either queues action 0x553/0x554 and records it on the unit, or subtracts the action's power from the unit and returns 1.
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named (Battle_QueueActionEx, Battle_ActionRecord_GetPower, 0x0063FD24 action rows), which supports 'HP change', but the direction (damage vs heal) and the meaning of the 0x553/0x554 actions are still open, and the only caller is the maybe_ Battle_Ui_LoadPartyModelResources.

name: Field_Object_Kind12_Ctor
summary: Constructor of field object kind 12: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x777760, sets the two default words at 0x497/0x498 and resets the party member slot.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind12, whose disassembly shows both allocation branches calling this one constructor; the body stores vtable 0x777760, not the 0x777348 the old name claimed.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReleaseRecords
summary: Releases an overlay's records: it clears the f_44 entries at +0x2C, sets the scene node's +0x7D flag, returns the 57 0x30-byte records at +0x58 to the scene node through Gfx_Trail_PushSample and finishes with 0x00239A1C.
evidence: No caller; the body's only certain effects are the f_44 entry clear, the scene-node flag and the 57-record return loop, so the old 'ScreenSlideAnim_Stop' name asserted a class the code does not show - the same shape also appears at 0x4CD9B0 under a different label.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the horse-race window: installs the class vtable, releases the f_44 entry objects at +0x2C, zeroes the count, runs the widget base destructor and frees the block.
evidence: The body ends in the widget base destructor and the free helper, so the deleting-destructor role is certain; the class still rests only on the neighbouring horse-race code (Ui_UmaWindow_ReleaseRows and friends), so the 'UmaWindow' part stays a guess.

name: AnimObject_UpdateAttachmentPoint
summary: Per-frame update of an animated object's attachment point: advances the attachment height by f_A4 clamped to [0, f_52C] (or keeps the fixed offset when the 0x007A6088 flag is set), samples the pose, blends the transforms, converts the local offset to world space and writes the resulting position at self+4/+8/+0xC. Returns 1.
evidence: NEW: the body writes the world position at self+4/+8/+0xC from the base position plus the blended local offset, and the alternate branch uses the fixed offset at +0x548; the named callees Anim_BlendTransform and Math_BuildBoundsFromSphereAndOffset are the pose blend and the local-to-world conversion.

name: maybe_Ui_SidePanel_PlaySideAnim
summary: Plays the side-panel transition: one branch calls Ui_Widget_PlaySideIn on the panel and on f_1224, the other calls Ui_Widget_PlaySideOut on f_11D4 and starts the 'side_out' animation on f_1228, storing the handle at f_1270.
evidence: The body is damaged (in_ZR, unaff_r4): the branch condition is gone and Ui_PlayAnimByName is even called with the extra unaff_r4 argument, so which direction runs cannot be read; both halves are visible, so the old 'PlayOut' name was wrong to name only one.

name: Field_Object_SetPresentFlag
summary: Sets the object header byte +0x10 to 1, then clears it again when the Field2D manager's +0x74 record has bit 11 of its +0x1A word set. Shared by the field-object and battle-unit initialisers.
evidence: NEW: seven of the nine callers are the named Field_Object2D_InitDefault/InitMesh/InitSprite and the Field_BattleTrigger constructors, so the byte belongs to the shared field-object header rather than to a battle unit; the deciding test 0x0066AAB4 is a one-instruction bit-11 test of the Field2D manager's +0x74 record.

name: Ui_UmaWindow_OpenResultPage
summary: Opens the result page of the horse-race window: mode 3 selects state 8 (or 7), mode 4 selects state 9 (or 7); it then sets message arguments 5 (member name) and 6 (selection value) and starts the sub-window at +0x73C with that state.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Ui_UmaWindow_ReleaseRows fixes the class, and the body's mode-to-state mapping plus the two Message_SetArg calls (5 = the member name from 0x0035EB98, 6 = the selection) are fully readable.

name: Field_Object_Type1352_Ctor
summary: Constructor of field object type 1352: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x77A51C, sets the two default words at 0x497/0x498 and resets the party member slot.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Type1352, whose disassembly shows both allocation branches calling this one constructor, so it is the type's single constructor; the stored vtable 0x77A51C matches the old name's suffix, only the wording changes.

name: FieldParty_Kind10_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the FieldParty-derived object of scene kind 10: runs FieldParty_Ctor, installs vtable 0x77A630 and the 0x769850 sub-table, and clears the five id/handle words at +0xDE10..+0xDE20.
evidence: NEW: the base is the confident FieldParty_Ctor (0.72), not Ui_Screen_CtorBase, and the named caller Field_ObjectFactory_Kind10 picks this constructor when its third argument is non-zero while the other variant is the confident Battle_ActionSequence_Ctor - so the old 'Ui_ScreenCtor' name was wrong about the class.

name: Ui_ScreenObject_Ctor_77F34C
summary: Constructor of the second 0x1800-byte script/UI object of scene kind 16: runs Ui_ScreenObject_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x77F34C and the 0x769850 sub-table, and clears the id/handle fields through +0x1816.
evidence: NEW: the base is the confident Ui_ScreenObject_CtorBase (0.50) and the only caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind16, which picks this constructor when its third argument is non-zero and the twin 0x005A5F90 (same body, vtable 0x77F1DC) otherwise; the stored vtable 0x77F34C matches the name.

name: maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateIdleCommand
summary: Sends a command to the actor behind a model: after the state query (virtual +0xE8 with 0xDA) and the f_33 branch, it resolves the actor with Menu_FindActorByHandle, picks a pose group with Battle_SelectPoseGroup and sends it through 0x005E7848 (command 0x49 on the f_33 branch).
evidence: NEW: the named callees Menu_FindActorByHandle and Battle_SelectPoseGroup confirm that a command is sent to the actor, but nothing names the command or the 0x2D-frame timer, so the 'idle' reading stays a guess.

name: Field_Object_Kind46_Ctor
summary: Constructor of field object kind 46: runs Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x77BA38, sets the two default words at 0x497/0x498 and resets the party member slot.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind46, whose disassembly shows both allocation branches calling this one constructor; the stored vtable 0x77BA38 matches the old name's suffix, only the wording changes.

name: maybe_Fs_Request_WaitForService
signature: void maybe_Fs_Request_WaitForService(FsRequest* req, int service, int method)
summary: Issues a service-object call for a file request and waits on the completion gate: a negative result is formatted into the request, otherwise it clears the request and spins until the service publishes its reply.
evidence: The callers (Fs_Request_Build, Svc_AcClient_Cmd0004) and callees (Svc_Object_InvokeAndStoreResult, Fs_FormatResultCode) fit the 'invoke then wait' reading, but the wait loop itself decompiled to bad instruction data with 25 unreachable blocks, so the wait condition cannot be read.

name: Fs_CompleteServiceRequest
signature: void Fs_CompleteServiceRequest(FsResult* out, int* request, int* outValue, int value)
summary: File-service request wrapper: rejects a request whose first two words are zero with error 0xE0A13882, issues the 0x00501F3C service command, writes its reply minus one to *outValue and reports the status through Fs_FormatResultCode.
evidence: NEW: the body is fully readable and both error paths go through the confident Fs_FormatResultCode, while the request itself is issued by 0x00501F3C next to the named Svc_Ipc_SendThreeParams; the old Gfx_Pica_SetScissorRect name described a different subsystem and was already replaced.

name: Svc_Object_ReleaseHandleB
summary: Second copy of the service-object handle release: if the word at +4 holds a handle it releases the shared lock when bit 0 is set, frees the handle and clears the word. Returns the object for chaining.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x00504018 is now the confident Svc_Object_ReleaseHandleA (0.50) with the same body, and this copy's callers are the same kind of paths (Save_LoadSlotData, Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPathA/B), so the 'B' copy is confirmed.

name: Snd_StartChannelTransferThread
signature: unsigned Snd_StartChannelTransferThread(Sound_DspChannel* self, unsigned buffer, unsigned size, unsigned* timeout)
summary: Starts the DSP transfer thread of a sound channel: it resets the two light events, fills the thread attribute block and calls Os_CreateThreadWithStack with entry 0x00518768 and the buffer/size/timeout arguments, then stores the sign of the result at f_E.
evidence: NEW: the body calls the confident Os_CreateThreadWithStack with entry 0x00518768 and never waits, so the old 'WaitForDspFrame' name described the wrong half; the only caller is the named Snd_StartVoicePlayback.

name: maybe_Sound_SubmitAdpcmFrame
signature: unsigned maybe_Sound_SubmitAdpcmFrame(unsigned char* samples, unsigned arg2, int params, int channel, int count)
summary: Packs one ADPCM frame for the DSP: splits eight sample bytes into sixteen nibbles, combines them with the channel's predictor/step values from the parameter block and writes the result, then waits for the DSP event.
evidence: The packing loop is readable, but the body is damaged (unaff_r5, bad instruction data, a bogus func_0x005d1f7a target and an Os_CreateThreadWithStack call that cannot belong here), so the frame layout cannot be re-verified; the named caller Sound_SubmitAdpcmBlocks carries the same role name.

name: Snd_AdvanceFrameCounter
summary: Polls one audio-transfer slot: it waits on the slot's sync handle (svcWaitSynchronization1) and, when a full frame period has elapsed, cancels the wait, bumps the slot's frame byte at +0x131D and reports true; otherwise it reports false and leaves the slot alone.
evidence: NEW: the two named callers Sound_GetDisplayTime and Sound_WaitForDisplayTime are exactly the per-transfer frame tick users, and the body's svc 0x24 (svcWaitSynchronization1, per FACTS.md) plus the +0x131D increment show it advances the transfer frame, not a graphics frame.
